inherited_methods.method: Trivial Mertens summation over all primes p<=n
inherited_methods.loss_step: Forget the condition p does not divide binomial(2n,n).
inherited_methods.lost_information: Every base-p digit of n must lie in the lower half of the digit alphabet.
inherited_methods.consequence: Gives only (1+o(1)) log log n instead of an absolute constant.

inherited_methods.method: First-moment and second-moment estimates over n
inherited_methods.loss_step: Average the carry-free predicate over n before controlling exceptional simultaneous congruences.
inherited_methods.lost_information: The rare n on which many small primes are simultaneously carry-free, which are exactly the uniform problem.
inherited_methods.consequence: Proves f(n) tends to a constant for almost all n but supplies no pointwise ceiling.

inherited_methods.loss_step: Use only n mod p and ignore all lower prime ranges where several base-p digits occur.
inherited_methods.lost_information: The nested residue restrictions n mod p^j < p^j/2 for j>=2.
inherited_methods.consequence: Controls the large-prime tail by a constant but leaves a possible log log n contribution from small primes.

inherited_methods.method: Independent union bounds over prime-power scales
inherited_methods.loss_step: Charge the same carry-free prime once for every admissible power p^j.
inherited_methods.lost_information: Nestedness of the lower-half residue conditions and incompatibility across different prime bases.
inherited_methods.consequence: Introduces a log n/log p multiplicity and cannot yield a summable all-scale estimate.

inherited_methods.loss_step: Modify a number until it is simultaneously good in two fixed bases under the sharp sum-of-digit-density condition.
inherited_methods.lost_information: The proof is existential for two fixed bases and gives no quantitative obstruction when the number and reciprocal mass of the prime bases grow.
inherited_methods.consequence: Pairwise incompatibility is rigorously impossible: any two fixed odd primes are simultaneously carry-free for infinitely many n. A uniform upper bound must begin with genuinely many-base, weighted information.

required_new_information: A unique or weighted assignment of each carry-free prime to one prime-power scale with total reciprocal charge O(1).
A pointwise incompatibility principle for simultaneous lower-half residues in different prime-power moduli, not an average-in-n statement.
An exact adversarial CRT search showing which apparent independence or tensorization claims fail.
Uniform treatment of short terminal intervals where analytic prime-counting bounds lose strength.
A many-base theorem consistent with the EGRS infinite two-prime construction; pairwise correlation bounds cannot suffice.
